### Why part (b.1) is infeasible AS WRITTEN — the plan is internally contradictory

The plan's (b.1) corroboration signal is **structurally unavailable at the point the downgrade runs**, so the downgrade can NEVER fire — which makes acceptance criterion 6 unsatisfiable AND contradicts plan §11.

**The mechanism (`decide_session_stalled`, scripts/autonomous_session_watch.py:1049-1058):** the stalled detector trips a `respawn` action ONLY when BOTH signals are stale:
- line 1049: self-report fresh (`< window_s`) -> return `("keep", 0)`
- line 1055/1058: `marker_stale = marker_age is None or marker_age >= window_s`; `if not marker_stale: return ("keep", 0)`

So a `respawn` (the action the b.1 block rewrites) is reachable ONLY when `marker_age >= window_s` (the latest non-watcher work-marker is STALE) — there is no respawn to downgrade while the marker is fresh.

**The plan's b.1 downgrade (§4 b.1 pseudocode + §11):** downgrade `respawn -> alert` ONLY when `work_fresh = (marker_age < LIVE_WORK_CORROBORATION_S)`, AND §11 fixes `LIVE_WORK_CORROBORATION_S == STALLED_WINDOW_S` with "NO new env var / no second knob".

With `LIVE_WORK_CORROBORATION_S == STALLED_WINDOW_S`, `work_fresh` (`marker_age < window`) is the exact NEGATION of the trigger precondition (`marker_age >= window`). The two conditions are mutually exclusive, so `work_fresh` is ALWAYS False at the b.1 check point. Consequence: the downgrade fires NEVER; EVERY live-id stalled session respawns. That is behaviorally identical to NOT having (b.1) — the "do not respawn a live, working session" guarantee in the Goal is not delivered for the marker-stale case (the only case that reaches the code).

**The acceptance criterion that proves it:** criterion 6 demands "stale markers ... AND a recent non-watcher work-marker (within LIVE_WORK_CORROBORATION_S) -> ZERO respawns + one alert." With the windows EQUAL, "stale markers" (>= window) and "a recent work-marker" (< window) cannot both hold for one value. Criterion 6 is unsatisfiable under §11. I wrote criterion 6/7/11 tests against the implemented b.1 block and they fail exactly here: a fresh 5-min marker makes `decide_session_stalled` return `keep` (never respawn), so no alert ever fires; a stale 90-min marker reaches respawn but `work_fresh` is False, so it respawns (never downgrades). The downgrade branch is dead code.

### Root cause: the wrong Option was chosen

The plan §11 explicitly REJECTED **Option A (bounded K-escalation counter)** in favor of **Option B (work-marker corroboration)**. But Option B's only corroboration signal (`marker_age`) is degenerate at the trigger point — by construction the marker is already stale there. Every signal available when the trigger fires (self-report-stale, marker-stale, live-id-present) FAILS to distinguish the two cases (b.1) must separate:
- a genuinely-working-but-quiet LIVE session (downgrade to alert), vs
- a #506 dead-bg-chain LIVE session (must respawn).

A signal that CAN distinguish them is a NEW one not derivable from the staleness ages at trigger time — e.g. exactly Option A's per-episode escalation counter (alert first, escalate to respawn after K live-and-still-stale episodes), which IS available (`respawn_count` / a new counter persisted in `stalled-<N>.json`). The reconciler-preferred "simpler" Option B is the one that does not actually work; Option A (the rejected one) is the one that closes the #506 hole without a degenerate signal.

### Two plausible re-plan resolutions (NOT picked — for the re-planner)

1. **Switch to Option A (bounded K-escalation).** On a tripped trigger with a LIVE id, ALERT (not respawn) for the first K consecutive stale episodes; escalate to the canonical respawn on the (K+1)th. A persistently-live-but-dead-bg session (#506) is still eventually recovered (after K episodes); a transiently-quiet-but-live session that resumes self-reporting clears before K. Uses a per-episode counter in `stalled-<N>.json` (the plan already persists `respawn_count` / `alerted` there), available at trigger time.

2. **Keep Option B but make `LIVE_WORK_CORROBORATION_S` STRICTLY GREATER than `STALLED_WINDOW_S`** (a real second knob, e.g. `EPM_LIVE_WORK_CORROBORATION_MIN`, default 2x). Then there is a non-empty band `STALLED_WINDOW_S <= marker_age < LIVE_WORK_CORROBORATION_S` where the marker is stale-enough-to-trip yet fresh-enough-to-corroborate. This directly contradicts plan §11's "windows equal, no second knob", so it is a §11 amendment, not an implementation choice.

Either is a science/scoping call on the recovery policy that I must not make unilaterally (CLAUDE.md autonomous-mode plan-contradiction rule: route a self-defeating plan back to `/adversarial-planner`, do not paper over it). Part (b.2) (`STALLED_WINDOW_S` 45->60 + env tunable) is sound and independent of this contradiction; it can land in the re-plan.
